title: What Is a Robot? Components and the Sensing-Acting Loop

contract.reader: A student or engineer with no robotics background (feedback from the control series, torque and inertia assumed) starting the robotics series
contract.problem: "Robot" is used loosely; the reader needs a precise working definition and a shared vocabulary for the parts of a robot and how they interact before kinematics and estimation
contract.outcome: State what makes a machine a robot and place it on the autonomy spectrum; name the four subsystems; count degrees of freedom and mobility and use redundant, underactuated and nonholonomic; compute transmission torque, speed, reflected inertia and encoder resolution; explain the energy and information paths, the loop hierarchy and the three software architectures
contract.contribution: One structural picture (subsystems, two flows, loops within loops, software layers) tying hardware to control timing, with worked numbers and exercises; the point that a motor encoder's resolution does not describe the link
contract.evidence: Worked formulas and three exercises with answers; ISO 8373:2012 and :2021; Brooks (1986); Gat (1998); Nilsson, Ed. (1984)
contract.limitations: No kinematics, dynamics or estimation (entries 2 to 4); loop rates are orders of magnitude; software architectures described historically, not compared in depth

history.note: live review: accepted (editorial/live-reviews/article/what-is-a-robot.md); library decision: retain
